claim_being_audited: The actor recommends certifying the model only with explicit model-card disclosure of the small-business support slice weakness, and without relying on an unapproved mitigation draft, on the theory that aggregate performance clears the deployment threshold while subgroup weakness remains materially disclosable.
specific_concerns: The role has only the actor's summary and citation list, not the underlying contents of the cited evidence.
The actor asserts exact threshold margins and slice gaps, but no underlying evaluation tables, confidence intervals, or model-card text are available to verify them.
The policy predicate that the slice weakness is 'material' is plausible from the summary but not independently established by admissible source content.
The claim that the mitigation is unapproved is central to the recommendation, but no approval record or policy-linked approval status is provided directly to the auditor.
The recommendation may be directionally consistent with policy, but the packet appears to overstate evidential support relative to what is actually available to this role.
unsupported_claims: That the model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
That the small-business support slice is exactly 1.1 percentage points below its warning threshold and 2.6 points below its preferred threshold.
That the proposed mitigation is in fact unapproved.
That the cited evidence, as opposed to the actor's summary, establishes all predicates needed for certification with disclosure.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-010-A through BMCARD-010-E, especially the evaluation results, threshold definitions, and model-card disclosure language.
Provide the approval-status record for the proposed mitigation draft.
Provide the policy or rubric used to determine when a subgroup weakness is material for certification purposes.
Provide the sampling note or confidence-interval analysis for the small-business support slice.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if a material weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not negate subgroup weakness.
Small-sample uncertainty may justify follow-up but does not by itself resolve an unresolved materiality question.
Exact performance and approval-status claims require direct evidentiary support, not only actor characterization.
